_comment: Judge roster. Set COVENANT_JUDGE_PROVIDERS to the names you want.
_why_three: build_semantic_quorum sets min_agree=1 and decides by MAJORITY VETO:
threshold = ceil(n * 0.5) dissents blocks. A judge that RAISES --
unreachable, timed out, model unloaded -- counts as a dissent.
n=1  threshold 1   one judge fails -> every transaction rejected
n=2  threshold 1   one judge fails -> every transaction rejected
n=3  threshold 2   one judge fails -> chain keeps running
So TWO judges is strictly worse than one: two things that can each
unilaterally halt the chain. Verified by killing one: with 3 a benign
gift was ADMITTED; with 2 the same gift was REJECTED.
The useful corollary: at 2-of-3 a WEAK judge is safe. It cannot block a
legitimate transfer alone and cannot approve theft alone. So the third
vote can be a small fast model -- which is what makes this affordable.
_why_a_size_ladder: Measured per verdict: qwen3:8b 60s, qwen3:4b 34s, qwen3:1.7b 15s.
A ladder costs 109s per transaction; three 8b's cost ~180s. Same
fault tolerance, 40% less work, and the models differ -- which is real
reasoning diversity, not the label diversity QuorumJudge warns about.
_required_ollama_setting: OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS must be >= the number of DISTINCT models here.
At 1, each judge evicts the previous and pays a full reload: measured
13.7s + 7.3s + 2.7s = 23.7s of pure reload PER TRANSACTION. Three
models is 9.1GB resident, which fits 16GB with room to spare.
_places: All three below are on one machine, so they share ONE failure: that
machine. Model diversity is real; location diversity is not, yet.
For actual location diversity, point one entry at a second machine over
Tailscale -- same file, just a different url. See PHONE_NODE.md.
